svg.text: Each step depends on the ones above it. The setup_workspace job automates the full sequence.

Step 1. Unity Catalog catalog + schema CREATE SCHEMA <catalog>.<schema>. Volumes for knowledge corpus and artifacts. Everything else lives in here. If this fails: you lack CREATE SCHEMA grant on the catalog. Ask a UC admin.

Step 2. Data tables Mode = synthetic: the data_generator builds patients/diagnoses/etc. with Faker (healthcare only). Mode = existing_uc_schema: you load your own domain tables into the schema before this step (see FORK_GUIDE).

Step 3. Knowledge corpus drop into UC Volume Your reference docs go in /Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<corpus>/. Setup chunks them and writes to the AI Search index. Domain spec field: knowledge.source_volume_path

Step 4. Vector Search endpoint + hybrid index Endpoint creation can take ~10 minutes on a cold workspace. Index reads from the chunked corpus table. If this fails: VS endpoint quota or wrong region. Domain spec field: ontology.source.index_name

Step 5. Lakebase instance + database (optional) Postgres-backed chat thread store. Skip with --var minimal=true if Lakebase is unavailable; sessions then live in memory. Lakebase does not support OBO; the App SP connects via the postgres resource binding.

Step 6. Agent on Model Serving log_model with AuthPolicy (SystemAuthPolicy for SP-grants, UserAuthPolicy for OBO scopes). Register in UC. agents.deploy. If this fails: warehouse CAN_USE missing, or unity-catalog scope conflict. Check the Serving Endpoint UI for the deployment_state_message.

Step 7. Databricks App FastAPI frontend bound to warehouse + agent endpoint + Lakebase via typed AppResource bindings. user_api_scopes: sql, serving.serving-endpoints (so the App can forward an OBO token to the agent).

Domain spec domains/<name>/domain.yaml
This one file drives: + Step 2 table names + Step 3 corpus path + Step 4 index name + Step 6 agent prompt + tools + Step 6 SQL guardrails
Bundle var: --var domain=<name>
Fork? Change here only.
